subject.title: [Feature]: Per-agent cost budget enforcement at the gateway level

question: Should OpenClaw add native per-agent spend-budget enforcement in the gateway, or should spend caps remain a plugin/external-supervisor responsibility using the existing pre-run hook surface?
rationale: The request adds config/default surface, persistent accounting/reservation semantics, provider dispatch policy, and operator UX in a stable gateway area; source proves the gap but does not decide the product boundary.

options.title: Add a narrow core budget gate
options.body: Design a canonical config and durable pre-dispatch admission/reservation path with clear reset windows, structured over-budget outcomes, and status/doctor reporting.

options.title: Keep enforcement outside core
options.body: Document before_agent_run and ClawHub/plugin patterns as the supported budget-enforcement path, adding only missing generic hook metadata if maintainers identify a specific API gap.

options.title: Split into narrower guardrails
options.body: Leave this as design discussion while cron maxSpend, failover ceilings, and session/run caps land separately under their own focused issues.

recommendation.title: Add a narrow core budget gate
recommendation.body: Design a canonical config and durable pre-dispatch admission/reservation path with clear reset windows, structured over-budget outcomes, and status/doctor reporting.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced adjacent cost reporting and runtime guardrail behavior and is the strongest history-backed product-boundary routing candidate in this review.
